points.point: LLMLingua (perplexity-based token deletion with a small LM) keeps GSM8K exact match at 79.08 at 5x and 77.33 at 20x, against 78.85 for the full 2,366-token prompt, so 20x costs about 1.5 points.
points.paper: library/llm/context/LLMLingua. Compressing Prompts for Accelerated Inference of Large Language Models.md
points.evidence: Table 2 (p. 5–6): Full-shot 78.85 / 2,366 tokens; Ours 79.08 at 446 tokens (5x); Ours 77.33 at 117 tokens (20x).

points.point: LLMLingua degrades much faster on BBH: from 70.07 full-shot to 61.60 at 5x and 56.85 at 7x (about 8.5 and 13.2 points lost).
points.paper: library/llm/context/LLMLingua. Compressing Prompts for Accelerated Inference of Large Language Models.md

points.point: All methods, LLMLingua included, drop sharply at around 25–30x compression on GSM8K.
points.paper: library/llm/context/LLMLingua. Compressing Prompts for Accelerated Inference of Large Language Models.md
points.evidence: Limitations (p. 9, Figure 3): 'around 25x-30x, all methods as well as ours will experience a substantial performance drop'.

points.point: LLMLingua's ablation: removing iterative token-level compression or the budget controller costs about 5–6 EM each, while removing distribution alignment to the target LLM costs about 0.5.
points.paper: library/llm/context/LLMLingua. Compressing Prompts for Accelerated Inference of Large Language Models.md
points.evidence: Table 3 (§5.4, p. 7): Ours 79.08; w/o Iterative Token-level Compression 72.93; w/o Budget Controller 73.62; w/o Distribution Alignment 78.62.

points.point: Asking GPT-4 to rewrite the prompt shorter does worse than LLMLingua, because the generated prompt omits reasoning steps.
points.paper: library/llm/context/LLMLingua. Compressing Prompts for Accelerated Inference of Large Language Models.md
points.evidence: Table 2: GPT4 Generation 71.87 (GSM8K, 5x) and 27.13 (BBH, 3x) against 79.08 and 70.11. §5.3 (p. 6): generated prompts 'may omit crucial details from the original prompt, particularly reasoning steps'.

points.point: Simply keeping one demonstration already scores 77.10 on GSM8K at 6x (422 tokens), so much of LLMLingua's 20x headline reflects redundant few-shot demonstrations.
points.paper: library/llm/context/LLMLingua. Compressing Prompts for Accelerated Inference of Large Language Models.md
points.evidence: Table 2: 1-shot 77.10, 422 tokens, 6x, against Full-shot 78.85. The numbers are the paper's; the redundancy reading is the answers' own inference.

points.point: LLMLingua's latency gain trails its token saving: 5x fewer tokens gives a 3.3x end-to-end speedup on GSM8K.
points.paper: library/llm/context/LLMLingua. Compressing Prompts for Accelerated Inference of Large Language Models.md
points.evidence: Table 6 (p. 8): end-to-end 8.6 s without compression; 2.3 s (3.3x) at 5x; 4.9 s (1.7x) at 2x; 1.3 s (5.7x) at 10x.

points.point: LongLLMLingua makes compression question-aware: it ranks documents by how well each predicts the question, scores tokens by how much the question changes their perplexity, reorders documents against lost-in-the-middle, and restores entity names with subsequence recovery.
points.paper: library/llm/context/LongLLMLingua. Accelerating and Enhancing LLMs in Long Context Scenarios via Prompt Compression.md
points.evidence: §4.1 (p. 3) question-aware coarse-grained compression using p(x^que | x^doc) and question-aware fine-grained compression; §4.2 (p. 4) document reordering; §4.4 (p. 5) subsequence recovery of entities in the response.

points.point: On NaturalQuestions (20 documents, GPT-3.5-Turbo) at 4x with the gold document in 10th position, LongLLMLingua scores 71.2 against 54.1 for the original prompt; the headline '21.4%' boost is 21.4 points, 75.5 with reordering against 54.1.
points.paper: library/llm/context/LongLLMLingua. Accelerating and Enhancing LLMs in Long Context Scenarios via Prompt Compression.md
points.evidence: Table 1 (p. 5–6), 4x: LongLLMLingua 10th = 71.2, Reorder = 75.5; Original Prompt 10th = 54.1. Main results (p. 6): 'a performance boost of 21.4% on NaturalQuestions with the ground-truth document at the 10th position' at about 4x fewer tokens.

points.point: Question-blind compression (LLMLingua, Selective-Context) scores below the 56.1 zero-shot result on NaturalQuestions: LLMLingua gets roughly 37–42 at 2x and 23.5–30 at 4x.
points.paper: library/llm/context/LongLLMLingua. Accelerating and Enhancing LLMs in Long Context Scenarios via Prompt Compression.md
points.evidence: Table 1: LLMLingua 2x = 39.7/39.5/40.4/37.1/42.3; 4x = 25.5/27.5/23.5/26.5/30.0; Selective-Context 19.5–45.4; Zero-shot 56.1. Main results (p. 6) says these are 'worse than the zero-shot setting'. Quoted ranges are slightly loose: the 2x low is 37.1, not 39.7, and the 4x low is 23.5, not 25.5.

points.point: LongLLMLingua's gain is mostly document selection or reranking: its ranker alone gets 69.3 on NQ (4x, 10th position) against 71.2 for the full method, and 46.3 against 48.3 on LongBench; without question-aware ranking it falls from 77.2 to 42.1, while without question-aware token pruning it falls only to 75.8.
points.paper: library/llm/context/LongLLMLingua. Accelerating and Enhancing LLMs in Long Context Scenarios via Prompt Compression.md
points.evidence: Table 1, 4x: LongLLMLingua r_k 10th = 69.3. Table 2, 2,000 tokens: r_k AVG 46.3, LongLLMLingua 48.3, Original 44.0. Table 3 (2x, 1st position): full 77.2; w/o Question-awareness 42.1; w/o Question-aware Fine-grained 75.8. 'Mostly reranking' is the answers' interpretation of these numbers.

points.point: With the gold document in first position, compression gives no accuracy gain: 75.0 for LongLLMLingua against 75.7 for the original prompt, so the 'compression improves accuracy' result is largely a lost-in-the-middle fix.
points.paper: library/llm/context/LongLLMLingua. Accelerating and Enhancing LLMs in Long Context Scenarios via Prompt Compression.md
points.evidence: Table 1, 4x, GPT-3.5-Turbo, 1st position: LongLLMLingua 75.0, Original Prompt 75.7. The lost-in-the-middle reading is the answers' inference.

points.point: LongLLMLingua must recompress for every question, so the compressed context cannot be cached, and it costs twice LLMLingua's compute.
points.paper: library/llm/context/LongLLMLingua. Accelerating and Enhancing LLMs in Long Context Scenarios via Prompt Compression.md
points.evidence: Limitation (p. 9): 'requires re-compression for different questions, even with the same context, preventing caching of the context... increases the computation by twice as much as LLMLingua'.

points.point: LLMLingua-2 replaces perplexity scoring with a small bidirectional encoder (XLM-RoBERTa-large, 355M parameters) that classifies each token keep or drop, trained on GPT-4 extractive compressions of MeetingBank meeting transcripts.
points.paper: library/llm/context/LLMLingua-2. Data Distillation for Efficient and Faithful Task-Agnostic Prompt Compression.md
points.evidence: Abstract (p. 1): token classification with a Transformer encoder over full bidirectional context; §3 (p. 3–4) data distillation from GPT-4; Implementation details (p. 6): xlm-roberta-large, trained on MeetingBank; Appendix H (p. 14): 355M parameters.

points.point: On MeetingBank QA, LLMLingua-2 scores 86.92 EM at 3.1x against 87.75 for the original prompt and 67.52 for LLMLingua, but the comparison is not budget-matched (970 tokens against 1,176–1,222 at 2.5x for the baselines).
points.paper: library/llm/context/LLMLingua-2. Data Distillation for Efficient and Faithful Task-Agnostic Prompt Compression.md
points.evidence: Table 1 (p. 5): LLMLingua-2 86.92, 970 tokens, 3.1x; LLMLingua 67.52, 1,176 tokens, 2.5x; Selective-Context 66.28, 1,222 tokens, 2.5x; Original 87.75, 3,003 tokens.

points.point: LLMLingua-2's compressor is 3–6x faster than LLMLingua (0.4–0.5 s against 1.5–2.9 s), gives a 1.6–2.9x end-to-end speedup at 2–5x compression, and uses 2.1 GB of GPU memory against 16.6 GB.
points.paper: library/llm/context/LLMLingua-2. Data Distillation for Efficient and Faithful Task-Agnostic Prompt Compression.md
points.evidence: Table 5 (p. 8): LLMLingua-2 0.5/0.4/0.4 s, LLMLingua 2.9/2.1/1.5 s; end-to-end 9.4 s (1.6x), 7.5 s (2.1x), 5.2 s (2.9x) against 14.9 s. Abstract: '3x-6x faster'. Appendix I (p. 14): 2.1GB against 16.6GB.

points.point: On LongBench at a 2,000-token budget, LLMLingua-2 averages 39.1: above LLMLingua (34.6) but below the original prompt (44.0) and below question-aware LongLLMLingua (48.0), with the Synthetic subset at 21.3 against 37.8. The authors attribute the gap to ignoring the question.
points.paper: library/llm/context/LLMLingua-2. Data Distillation for Efficient and Faithful Task-Agnostic Prompt Compression.md
points.evidence: Table 2 (p. 6): LLMLingua-2 AVG 39.1, Synth. 21.3; LLMLingua 34.6; LongLLMLingua 48.0; Original Prompt AVG 44.0, Synth. 37.8. p. 8: it 'falls short when compared to other task-aware compression methods like LongLLMlingua... additional information that they leverage from the question'.

points.point: LLMLingua-2 only ties LLMLingua on GSM8K and BBH, and its out-of-domain baseline numbers are copied from the LongLLMLingua paper, not re-run.
points.paper: library/llm/context/LLMLingua-2. Data Distillation for Efficient and Faithful Task-Agnostic Prompt Compression.md
points.evidence: Table 3 (p. 6): GSM8K 79.08 against 79.08 (1-shot) and 77.79 against 77.41 (half-shot); BBH 70.02 against 70.11 and 61.94 against 61.60. Tables 2 and 3 captions: '†: numbers reported in Jiang et al. (2023b)'.

points.point: Adding LongLLMLingua's question-aware document-level (coarse-grained) compression to LLMLingua-2 gives an average gain of 25.3% on NaturalQuestions.
points.paper: library/llm/context/LLMLingua-2. Data Distillation for Efficient and Faithful Task-Agnostic Prompt Compression.md
points.evidence: Appendix K (p. 14), Table 11: 'LLMLingua-2 with LongLLMLingua coarse-grained compression achieves an average performance gain of 25.3% on NaturalQuestions compared to LLMLingua-2'.

points.point: RECOMP trains an extractive sentence selector and an abstractive summariser (distilled from a large LM) on the reader's end-task performance; the compressor can return an empty string when retrieval would not help.
points.paper: library/llm/context/RECOMP. Improving Retrieval-Augmented LMs with Compression and Selective Augmentation.md
points.evidence: Abstract (p. 1): both compressors 'trained to improve LMs' performance on end tasks'; 'our compressor can return an empty string, implementing selective augmentation'. §3.2 (p. 4): the abstractive compressor is distilled from a teacher model.

points.point: RECOMP's abstractive compressor reaches 37.04 EM on NQ with 36 tokens against 39.39 with 660 tokens of top-5 documents: about 5–6% of the tokens for about 2 EM lost.
points.paper: library/llm/context/RECOMP. Improving Retrieval-Augmented LMs with Compression and Selective Augmentation.md
points.evidence: Table 2 (p. 7): Top 5 documents 660 tokens / 39.39 EM; abstractive Ours 36 tokens / 37.04 EM. p. 7: 'a compression ratio of 5% tokens while losing 2 EM points'. Abstract: 'as low as 6% with minimal loss'.

points.point: Compression removes distractors: with five full documents the reader copies a wrong span from the evidence 81% of the time, with RECOMP's summary 39%, and with GPT-3.5 summaries 85%.
points.paper: library/llm/context/RECOMP. Improving Retrieval-Augmented LMs with Compression and Selective Augmentation.md
points.evidence: Table 3 and §6 (p. 8): 'Prepending top 5 documents has a higher frequency (81%) of copying incorrectly... GPT-3 compression leads to an even higher incorrect copying frequency (85%)... Our compressor successfully reduce such erroneous behavior to 39%.'

points.point: An oracle single sentence reaches 60.22 EM on NQ against 39.39 for five full documents, so the headroom is in selection and the trained compressors are far below it.
points.paper: library/llm/context/RECOMP. Improving Retrieval-Augmented LMs with Compression and Selective Augmentation.md
points.evidence: Table 2 (p. 7): extractive Oracle 34 tokens / 60.22 EM; Top 5 documents 39.39; trained extractive 36.57, abstractive 37.04.

points.point: RECOMP is weaker on multi-hop HotpotQA: the abstractive compressor (28.20 EM) falls below a single uncompressed document (28.80), extraction does better (11% of tokens for −2.4 EM), only 67% of its HotpotQA summaries are faithful (30 samples judged by the authors), and the compressors transfer poorly to a different reader on QA.
points.paper: library/llm/context/RECOMP. Improving Retrieval-Augmented LMs with Compression and Selective Augmentation.md
points.evidence: Table 2: HotpotQA abstractive Ours 28.20, Top 1 document 28.80, extractive Ours 30.40, Top 5 32.80. p. 7: '11% compression rate while losing 2.4 EM points'. Table 4 (p. 9): HQA Ours 67% faithful against 74% for GPT-3.5, 30 samples, annotated by the authors. §6 (p. 8), transfer to LLaMA-13B: 'performance is worse than the LM from which compressors are trained on'.

points.point: Gisting changes the attention mask during instruction fine-tuning so later tokens see the prompt only through gist tokens; it reaches up to 26x compression (about 26-token instructions into one token) with near-parity quality (human win rate 52.3% for LLaMA-7B) and up to 40% fewer FLOPs.
points.paper: library/llm/context/Learning to Compress Prompts with Gist Tokens.md
points.evidence: Abstract and §1 (p. 1–2): attention-mask modification, 'up to 26x', 'up to 40% FLOPs reduction and 4.2% latency speedups'. §5 (p. 5): human eval on 100 examples, 'average win rates of 52.3% (vs. 48.0%) for LLaMA-7B'. §6 (p. 8): 'compressing 26 tokens into 1'.

points.point: Against ordinary KV caching of the full instruction, gisting saves only 0.11% of FLOPs and about 1% of wall time; the 40% figure is against no caching, and the real remaining gain is cache storage and context-window space.
points.paper: library/llm/context/Learning to Compress Prompts with Gist Tokens.md
points.evidence: §6 (p. 8), Table 3: 'a negligible decrease in FLOPs (0.11%) and a modest 1% speedup in wall time' when compared with caching the full instruction; 40% FLOPs savings are over unoptimized models; storage and context-window benefits are discussed in the same section.

points.point: Gisting fails when the instruction holds details that must be copied verbatim, such as a list of allowed categories.
points.paper: library/llm/context/Learning to Compress Prompts with Gist Tokens.md
points.evidence: §5.1 Failure cases (p. 7): 'when the instruction contains specific details, e.g. phrases that must be copied verbatim into the output', with the example 'Give the news title a category. Pick a category from the list of...'.

points.point: ICAE uses a LoRA-adapted encoder to write about 512 tokens into 128 memory slots (4x) for the LLM; at 4x, the compressed model wins 19.6% and loses 45.4% against the same Llama-2-7b-chat given the full context. Its slots do beat a 128-token GPT-4 summary about 2 to 1.
points.paper: library/llm/context/In-context Autoencoder for Context Compression in a Large Language Model.md
points.evidence: §3.1 (p. 4): LoRA on the encoder, k=128. Table 4 (p. 4–6): Llama-2-7b-chat (ICAE, k=128) against Llama-2-7b-chat: win 19.6, lose 45.4, tie 35.0. §3.2.2 (p. 6): 'still lags behind its counterpart conditioning on the original context'; memory slots beat 128-token GPT-4 summaries 'with ~2x win/lose ratio'.

points.point: ICAE's reconstruction is near-perfect for contexts up to about 300 tokens (BLEU 99.3 on normal text), declines beyond 400, and degrades sharply with fewer than 128 slots; the authors call more than 4x compression 'rather challenging'.
points.paper: library/llm/context/In-context Autoencoder for Context Compression in a Large Language Model.md
points.evidence: §3.2.1 (p. 4): 'When the context length is within 300, the ICAE can almost perfectly reconstruct... beyond 400, both BLEU and EM scores start to decline'; k=64 and 32 are 'much less satisfactory'; 'achieving over 4× compression is rather challenging'. Table 3: Normal text BLEU 99.3.

points.point: An independent test finds selection beats compression at a tight budget: on HotpotQA with a 160-token budget and a 3B reader, LLMLingua-2 scores 0.326 F1 against 0.400 for naive top-k packing and 0.451 for a submodular packer, because token dropping destroys the answer span.
points.paper: library/llm/context/Recall Is Not Enough. A Reader-Context Diagnostic for Budget-Constrained Retrieval-Augmented.md
points.evidence: Table 3 (§5, p. 6): llmlingua (compr.) 0.326, chunk_packed (naive) 0.400, chunk_submod 0.451; Qwen2.5-3B reader, budget 160. p. 6: submod beats it by +0.125 F1, naive by +0.075; 'token-level dropping destroys the answer span'. Answer J's details are off: the paper is dated 2026-07-01, not 2025, and the budget is 160 tokens (LLMLingua-2's output lands at about 130).

errors.quote: Old targets: the models are GPT-3.5, Claude-v1.3 and 7B Llamas
errors.paper_says: Not all of them. RECOMP's QA reader is Flan-UL2 (20B) with a transfer test on LLaMA-13B (p. 7 Table 2 caption; p. 8), Gisting also uses FLAN-T5-XXL (p. 1), and LLMLingua-2 also tests Mistral-7B (p. 8). The dating argument itself holds.

asis-q5-r2.comment: Every number and page I checked matches the papers, including the less obvious ones: ablation 72.93/73.62/78.62 against 79.08 (LLMLingua p. 7 Table 3), oracle sentence 60.2 against 39.3 (RECOMP p. 8 Table 3), SeCom 69.33 to 59.87 (p. 7 Table 2), ACE 18,282 to 122 tokens and 91.8% cache reuse (p. 3, p. 10), Cartridges 30 minutes on 8xH100 (p. 12). It reports LongLLMLingua's +21.4 at face value, without the position-1 parity (75.0 against 75.7) or the fact that the ranker alone gets most of the gain, and it omits the one-shot baseline (77.10) behind the 20x headline. Its statements about which papers have notes could not be checked, since this copy has no notes directory.

errors.quote: Selective-Context and AutoCompressors are cited as baselines by nearly every paper above
errors.paper_says: Selective-Context is a baseline only in the three LLMLingua papers. RECOMP's baselines are BM25, DPR, Contriever, T5 and GPT-3.5 (p. 7 Table 2); Gisting's are positive and negative controls and TF-IDF (p. 4, §4.2); ICAE and RECOMP cite AutoCompressors only as related work (ICAE p. 8 §4), not as a baseline. The second half of the sentence, that neither is in the library or the skip list, is correct.

errors.quote: the gist and ICAE results by ChatGPT or GPT-4 pairwise preference
errors.paper_says: Gisting also reports ROUGE-L and a human evaluation (p. 5, §4.3; human win rate 52.3% for LLaMA-7B, Table 2). Only ICAE's fine-tuned results rest on GPT-4 preference alone.

nonotes-q5-r1.comment: Broadest coverage, and the adjacent-paper claims check out: Recall Is Not Enough +0.125 and +0.075 F1 (p. 6), RLM 26% median against compaction (p. 1), LongMemEval fact compression (p. 1), DeepSeek-OCR 97% and 60% (p. 1), the Cartridges conversion issue, RECOMP 85% against 39% (p. 8). It repeats LongLLMLingua's '+21.4%' as the paper prints it, without the position or noting it is 21.4 points (54.1 to 75.5 with reordering), so I did not credit point 9. It gives few numbers for LLMLingua-2 and ICAE and says itself that numbers were not checked against the tables; the ones it gives are right.

errors.quote: the papers put the usable range at about 2–5x for most tasks and up to about 10x for extractive RAG compression. Beyond that, quality degrades fast.
errors.paper_says: No paper states this range, and the results contradict it. LLMLingua loses 1.52 EM on GSM8K at 20x and puts the sharp drop at 25–30x (p. 6; p. 9). RECOMP's abstractive compressor keeps about 5% of tokens (roughly 18x) for 2 EM lost on NQ, and its extractive one uses 37 of 660 tokens for 36.57 against 39.39 (p. 7, Table 2). In the other direction, BBH already loses 8.5 EM at 5x (LLMLingua p. 6).

asis+claude-sonnet-5-5-q5-r1.review_only: My note flags the evidence as vendor-run. The authors also wrote the baselines, and the out-of-domain baseline numbers are copied from earlier papers.
asis+claude-sonnet-5-5-q5-r1.misleading: Mildly. The '2–5x, up to 10x for extractive RAG' rule is presented as what the papers say, but it is the answer's own synthesis and conflicts with LLMLingua's and RECOMP's reported results. LLMLingua, LongLLMLingua, RECOMP and Gisting are described from abstracts only, so their claims ('20x with little loss', 'compression can improve accuracy', '6% with minimal loss') go untested.
asis+claude-sonnet-5-5-q5-r1.comment: The LLMLingua-2 and ICAE sections are accurate and specific: 86.92/67.52/87.75, 970 against 1,176–1,222 tokens, 39.1/44.0/48.0, Synthetic 21.3 against 37.8, 45.4% lose against 19.6% win. The copied baseline numbers it attributes to a note are confirmed by the dagger footnotes on LLMLingua-2 Tables 2 and 3 (p. 6). Points 1 and 21 are credited loosely, since it gives only the abstract-level claim. Gisting's '40% fewer FLOPs and 4.2% lower latency' is correct (p. 1), but it misses that the gain against KV caching is 0.11%. 'Only LLMLingua-2 and ICAE have notes' could not be checked, since this copy has no notes directory. `paperlib read` does exist.

errors.quote: On NaturalQuestions with 20 documents at 4x, LLMLingua scores 25.5–30.0
errors.paper_says: LongLLMLingua Table 1 (p. 6) gives LLMLingua at 4x as 25.5, 27.5, 23.5, 26.5 and 30.0 for gold positions 1, 5, 10, 15 and 20, so the range is 23.5–30.0. The answer took the first and last columns. The conclusion, below the 56.1 zero-shot score, is unaffected.

noreviews-q5-r1.comment: The most critical reading, and the only answer to state the three points that reframe the headlines: one demonstration already scores 77.10 at 422 tokens (LLMLingua Table 2), question-blind compression falls below zero-shot on NQ, and position 1 shows no gain (75.0 against 75.7). The other numbers I checked are right: Recall Is Not Enough 0.326/0.400/0.451 with Qwen2.5-3B (p. 6 Table 3), RECOMP 37.04 at 36 tokens against 39.39 at 660, RLM 0.1 against 58.0 and 70.5 against 91.3 (p. 6 Table 1), SeCom −9.46, LightMem 50–80% (p. 8), DeepSeek-OCR's caveat (p. 19). It gives no LLMLingua-2 quality numbers and leaves out the LLMLingua ablation, BBH and the 25–30x limit. Point 13 is credited for the caching half only. The T5 detail in RECOMP is on p. 5, just outside the cited p. 2–4, which I did not count as an error. The claim about missing notes and the denied write could not be checked.

errors.paper_says: Table 2 stops at 20x (quarter-shot). The 25–30x drop is in the Limitations section and Figure 3 on p. 9 of LLMLingua, not in Table 2 on p. 6.

errors.quote: Gist tokens reach 26x only on instructions of about 20 tokens, lose verbatim wording, and save just 1% wall time over ordinary KV caching ([p. 8]
errors.paper_says: The 26x figure is 26 tokens compressed into 1 (§6, p. 8: 'compressing 26 tokens into 1'; Appendix F gives a rate of 26 on the Human validation split), so the instructions are about 26 tokens, not 20. The verbatim-copy failure is in §5.1 on p. 7, not p. 8.

errors.quote: Its compressor transfers poorly to another model (p. 8).
errors.paper_says: Minor over-generalisation. RECOMP p. 8 says the compressors transfer well to GPT2-XL and GPT-J on language modelling; only the QA transfer to LLaMA-13B is poor (Table 10).

noreviews-q5-r2.comment: The most complete on the critical points: the one-demonstration baseline, the ranker-alone result, no gain with the gold document first, the oracle headroom and the latency gap. All checked numbers hold (39.7, 71.2 vs 54.1, 69.3, 75.7 vs 75.0, 37.0 vs 39.4 vs 60.2, 45.4 vs 19.6, SeCom 59.9 to 69.3, Cartridges 38.6x). It does not state the BBH loss, the LLMLingua ablation, the mechanisms of LongLLMLingua, LLMLingua-2 or RECOMP, or the 81% to 39% copying result. It says openly that it read only the abstract and introduction of 'Recall Is Not Enough'.

errors.quote: It has a sentence selector and a summariser distilled from a large LM, and either can return nothing when retrieval would not help.
errors.paper_says: Only the abstractive compressor does selective augmentation. RECOMP p. 8: 'We have not experimented selective compression with extractive compressor, fixing the number of prepended sentences for the entire dataset (1 for Wikitext, 1 for NQ/TQA, 2 for HotpotQA).'
The link path is wrong: the paper is at library/vision-and-multimodal/vision-language/, not under llm/, so the link does not resolve. The page and the 97% and 60% figures are right.

nonotes-q5-r2.comment: The best account of mechanisms, and its page citations for the core papers are correct. Points 6, 11 and 12 are stated as conclusions without the supporting numbers (77.10 with one demonstration, 69.3 for the ranker alone, 75.0 vs 75.7 with the gold document first). It repeats the paper's '+21.4%' without saying it is 21.4 points (75.5 vs 54.1), so point 9 is not credited. The 355M parameter count is cited to §4, p. 5, but is in Appendix H, p. 14. Selective-Context and AutoCompressors are indeed absent from the library. The Cartridges, LightMem and SeCom claims check out.

errors.quote: runs LLMLingua-2 against plain chunk selection at the same tight RAG budget of about 130 tokens
errors.paper_says: The budget is 160 reader tokens (Recall Is Not Enough, p. 6, Setup and Table 3). About 130 is the length LLMLingua-2's output lands at (129.6); the packers use 145–152.

errors.quote: **Compression can beat the full prompt.** LongLLMLingua and RECOMP both improve accuracy by removing distractors.
errors.paper_says: RECOMP's trained compressors score below the five full documents on all three QA sets (p. 7, Table 2): NQ 37.04 and 36.57 vs 39.39, TQA 58.68 and 58.99 vs 62.37, HotpotQA 28.20 and 30.40 vs 32.80. Only the oracle compressions beat the full documents. The same answer's table says RECOMP loses 2 EM.

nonotes-q5-r3.misleading: It presents 'compression can beat the full prompt' as a recurring finding and credits RECOMP with it, which the paper's numbers contradict. It also does not say that LongLLMLingua's gain is mostly reranking and disappears with the gold document first; it only cautions about old target models.
nonotes-q5-r3.comment: Otherwise accurate, with correct pages: 0.11% FLOPs, twice LLMLingua's compute, +25.3% in Appendix K on p. 14, ICAE reconstruction to about 300 tokens, 0.125 and 0.075 F1. It repeats '+21.4%' without saying it is points, so point 9 is not credited. 'BERT-size' is loose for LLMLingua-2: the main model is XLM-RoBERTa-large (355M), and only the -small variant is BERT-base size. It misses the one-demonstration baseline, the ablations, the oracle headroom and the HotpotQA weakness. It says openly that it read only the summary line of Cartridges.

errors.quote: The evidence is one self-built, GPT-4-judged benchmark, and it never compares against other compression methods.
errors.paper_says: ICAE does compare its 128 memory slots against a 128-token GPT-4 summary of the same context (Table 5, last row, and the text on pp. 6–7: win 34.1%, lose 17.6%, about 2x win/lose). It is true that it does not compare against Gist or AutoCompressor.

noreviews+claude-sonnet-5-5-q5-r1.review_only: My notes rate the evidence as vendor-run, with no variance reported and baseline numbers copied from an earlier paper.
noreviews+claude-sonnet-5-5-q5-r1.comment: What it states is accurate: the LLMLingua-2 numbers (0.4–0.5 s vs 1.5–2.9 s, 39.1 vs 34.6 vs 48.0, 21.3 vs 37.8), ICAE 19.6% vs 45.4%, Cartridges 38.6x and 26.4x, LightMem 68.64 vs 56.80 and the 73.2 tie with GLM-4.6. But it does not answer the question for four of the six core papers: LLMLingua, LongLLMLingua, RECOMP and Gist get one line each from their summaries, and 'Recall Is Not Enough' is not mentioned. It says so openly, so the reader is under-informed, not misled. It rests on notes, not the papers, and ends by asking whether to read the rest. The count of 14 excludes the two surveys it names but did not open.

errors.quote: Recall Is Not Enough (2026) reports that a budgeted evidence packer beats LLMLingua-2 at equal or lower token cost.
errors.paper_says: The comparison is at the same 160-token budget, but LLMLingua-2's context is the shorter one: 129.6 tokens against 145.5 for the packer (p. 6, Table 3). The paper's 'fewer tokens' claim is against naive and focused packing (about 145 vs 152), not against LLMLingua-2.

asis-q5-r3.review_only: SeCom's note records LOCOMO falling from 69.33 to 59.87 without it (p. 7, Table 2). That figure is from the note, not re-checked in the paper.
asis-q5-r3.comment: Every number checked for the six core papers matches the markdown, including 446 tokens, 77.10 at 6x, 23.5 and 69.3 on NQ at 4x, 39.1/48.0/44.0 on LongBench, 28.20 vs 28.80 on HotpotQA and 19.6/45.4 for ICAE. The ACE figures (18,282 to 122 tokens, 66.7 to 57.1, 63.7 baseline, p. 3) and the SeCom figure it flags as unchecked (69.33 to 59.87, p. 7, Table 2) are also correct. Points 8, 15, 16, 18, 25, 29 and 30 are stated only in part: for example, 15 gives the unequal-budget caveat without the scores, and 30 gives the finding without numbers, from the abstract and introduction as the answer says. The answer says ICAE and LLMLingua-2 come from notes; this library copy has no notes/ directory, so that could not be checked. Table pages follow the markdown headings; the PDFs place several tables one or two pages later, which I did not count as errors for any answer.

errors.paper_says: The 2x row for LLMLingua with GPT-3.5-Turbo is 39.7, 39.5, 40.4, 37.1 and 42.3 across the five gold positions, so the range is 37.1–42.3 (LongLLMLingua, Table 1). 39.7 is the 1st-position value, not the minimum.

asis-q5-r1.review_only: SeCom, from the LLMLingua group, finds removing it costs about 9 points (69.33 to 59.87; p. 7, Table 2, from the note). Also: "Cartridges match in-context quality at 38.6x less memory, but cost about 30 minutes on 8 H100s per corpus (p. 1, 12, from the note)."
asis-q5-r1.misleading: Mildly. The bolded summary says dropping text 'only reliably helps when it knows the question', but the answer's own table shows question-blind LLMLingua holding GSM8K at 20x and LLMLingua-2 near parity on MeetingBank. It also says vector methods 'reach higher ratios', while ICAE stops at 4x and Gisting's 26x is for roughly 26-token instructions. A reader could under-rate question-blind pruning on redundant prompts and over-rate soft compression.
asis-q5-r1.comment: Apart from the one range, the numbers match the papers: LongBench 46.3/48.3/44.0, RECOMP 81% to 39% and oracle 60.22, Gisting 0.11% against KV caching, Recall Is Not Enough 0.326/0.400/0.451 (p. 6, Table 3) and Beyond RAG 36.48 to 34.58 (p. 8, Table 3). Both figures it marks as from notes are correct in the papers: Cartridges 38.6x and about 30 minutes on an 8×H100 node, and SeCom 69.33 to 59.87. It misses the LLMLingua caveats (BBH, the 25–30x collapse, the ablation, the one-shot baseline), LongLLMLingua's no-caching cost, the LLMLingua-2 LongBench gap and RECOMP's HotpotQA weakness. Point 12 is given as its own reading without the 75.0 vs 75.7 figures; points 14, 18 and 20 are stated in part.

errors.quote: On NaturalQuestions, LLMLingua and Selective-Context score 25–44, below the 56.1 of no documents at all
errors.paper_says: With GPT-3.5-Turbo the two methods range from 19.5 (Selective-Context, 4x, 5th position) to 45.4 (Selective-Context, 2x, 1st position); LLMLingua's lowest is 23.5 (LongLLMLingua, Table 1). All are below 56.1, so the conclusion holds, but the stated range is wrong at both ends.

errors.quote: Everything is measured on GPT-3.5, Claude-v1.3, LLaMA-7B or Flan-UL2 with 4k–16k windows.
errors.paper_says: Several results use other models: Gisting also uses FLAN-T5-XXL (p. 4), LLMLingua-2 reports Mistral-7B as a target (p. 8, Table 4), LongLLMLingua reports LongChat-13b (Table 1), and ICAE's headline comparison is on Llama-2-7b-chat and Llama-2-13b-chat (Table 4). The point that all targets are 2023-era models still stands.

noreviews-q5-r3.comment: The most complete answer, and the only one to give the BBH drop, the LLMLingua ablation, the LongLLMLingua ablation (77.2 to 42.1 and 75.8), RECOMP's 67% faithfulness on 30 samples and the reason token dropping loses in Recall Is Not Enough. The outside claims check out: Beyond RAG 36.48 to 34.58 with 1,588 vs 1,979 tokens (p. 8, Table 3), SeCom 69.33 to 59.87 (p. 7, Table 2), Recursive Language Models' median 26% over compaction on GPT-5 (abstract), and Rethinking Memory's finding that context compression trails KV-cache methods (p. 15, Fig. 6). The survey's context-compression section (p. 25) names no token-pruning prompt compressor, and no Selective-Context, AutoCompressors or xRAG paper is in the library. Points 17 and 24 are stated in part (17 without the LongLLMLingua comparison, 24 without the 28.20 vs 28.80 result). It misses the one-shot baseline (6), the wrong-span copying result (22) and the first-position result (12).
